trigger_condition: credential_values contains assistant_ids with an empty list []
potential_consequence: ms_teams integration created/updated with zero linked assistants, defeating its purpose

trigger_condition: check_ms_teams_singleton runs against request.project_name, which is not verified to match the project of setting_id being updated
potential_consequence: attacker can update an ms_teams setting while sending a different project_name, bypassing the per-project singleton and assistant-ownership checks entirely

trigger_condition: two concurrent create requests for the same project both read no existing ms_teams row before either insert completes
guard_snippet: add a unique DB/ES constraint on (project_name, credential_type='MS_TEAMS') instead of relying on check-then-create
potential_consequence: race condition lets two ms_teams settings be created for the same project, violating the intended singleton

trigger_condition: request.project_name is None or empty string while credential_type is MS_TEAMS
potential_consequence: check_ms_teams_singleton and belongs_to_project run against a None/empty project key, letting unrelated requests collide or silently pass

trigger_condition: credential_values has multiple entries with key='assistant_ids'; only the first via next() is validated
guard_snippet: collect all cv.key=='assistant_ids' entries and reject if more than one is present
potential_consequence: a second, unvalidated assistant_ids entry could be persisted and used elsewhere without ever passing ownership validation

trigger_condition: assistant_ids list contains duplicate ids, e.g. ['a1','a1']
potential_consequence: duplicate assistant bindings silently persisted, inflating notification fan-out or downstream processing
